summary_paragraph: A man with advanced HIV/AIDS, chronic respiratory failure, tracheostomy, and PEG dependence was admitted from a skilled nursing facility due to tachycardia, dyspnea, and hypotension. He was found to have septic shock likely triggered by influenza A with superimposed pneumonia and a urinary tract infection caused by E. coli. He was temporarily reconnected to the ventilator for respiratory support but quickly weaned back to his baseline trach collar. His mental status, initially altered due to sepsis, returned to baseline. He was treated with cefepime for 10 days, Tamiflu for influenza, and oral vancomycin for C. diff prophylaxis. A PICC line was placed for outpatient antibiotic administration. He was discharged back to extended care with instructions to restart tamsulosin and follow up with his PCP.
problems: Influenza due to unidentified influenza virus with unspecified type of pneumonia
Acute and chronic respiratory failure, unspecified whether with hypoxia or hypercapnia
Chronic obstructive pulmonary disease with (acute) lower respiratory infection
Urinary tract infection, site not specified
Unspecified Escherichia coli [E. coli] as the cause of diseases classified elsewhere
